h2: Water Leak Repair Kuta & Legian – Fast, Local Service
intro: If your PDAM meter spins overnight or a water pump never stops, you likely need water leak repair in Kuta & Legian before the damage spreads. Decades-old pipes, salt-laden air, and heavy monsoon rain make this stretch one of Bali's most leak-prone areas. Bali Fix locates and fixes hidden leaks across Kuta, Legian, and surrounding lanes like Tuban and Jl. Padma.

sections.h3: Why Leaks Are So Common Here
sections.text: Kuta and Legian sit close enough to the beach that salt-laden air eats through brass mixers, copper joints, and steel drain pipes within a few seasons. Add decades of original plumbing from the guesthouse era, and you get a recipe for slow seepage behind tile walls or under concrete slabs. In low-lying lanes around Tuban and Jl. Padma, monsoon backflow also stresses floor drains and septic connections, turning small hairline cracks into full bursts by the next dry spell.

sections.h3: Typical Jobs We Handle in Guesthouses & Villas
sections.text: A ten-room guesthouse on Jl. Legian means ten toilets, ten mixers, ten water heaters all running daily. That volume wears out PPR joints, shower cartridges, and sink traps far faster than a single-family villa. The most common calls we get here involve a leak you can't see: the PDAM meter keeps rotating at night, or the pressure pump cycles every few minutes because water is escaping somewhere behind a wall or under a garden irrigation line. We trace it, cut out the damaged section, and rejoin with new fittings.

sections.h3: What to Send for an Accurate Quote
sections.text: Before we quote, send a short WhatsApp message with three things: a photo or video of where you notice dampness, drips, or a running pump; your exact address (street name plus landmark helps in Kuta's grid); and roughly when the problem started. If the leak is hidden—say, the meter spins but no visible drip exists—just describe that. No need to tear anything open first. The cost depends on what we find once we access the pipe, so every job gets its own estimate after inspection.

sections.h3: Preventing the Next Leak in a Beach-Side Area
sections.text: Because salt air accelerates corrosion on any exposed metal fitting, check your outdoor taps, shower valves, and garden hose bibs every two or three months for white-green residue or weeping threads. In Kuta's monsoon season, clear floor drains in bathrooms and kitchens before heavy rain hits; backed-up water is a leading cause of septic-line cracks in older Legian properties. And if you run an irrigation line through the garden, shut it off completely during dry months rather than leaving it pressurised.

faq.q: My PDAM meter keeps spinning at night but I can't find any drip. What's going on?
faq.a: That almost always means a hidden leak behind a wall, under a slab, or in a buried garden line. Send us a photo of the meter reading and your address on WhatsApp; we'll trace the source before giving you an estimate.

faq.q: How does being near the beach affect my plumbing?
faq.a: Salt-laden air accelerates corrosion on metal fittings well beyond what you'd see further inland. Mixers, drain traps, and outdoor taps in this stretch tend to wear out sooner, so regular visual checks save you from surprise bursts.

faq.q: Do I need to be home when you come for the inspection?
faq.a: Not necessarily—a villa manager or housekeeper with access is fine. Just make sure they can open the relevant cupboard, shower head, or pump enclosure so we can inspect without delay.
